active_paradigms.idea: Add unexplored symmetric polyhedral seed families: heptagonal antiprism (14 vertices, all-equal edges), heptagonal prism, gyroelongated structures, and the 14-vertex rhombic dodecahedron variants, then homotopy-refine them
active_paradigms.description: The current program's graph seeds are limited to 6+6+2 rings, icosahedron+caps, cuboctahedron+caps, and one rhombic dodecahedron wiring. A heptagonal antiprism has exactly 14 vertices, is vertex-transitive with two edge classes (side edges and top/bottom heptagon edges) — by tuning the heptagon radius r and height h you can make side edges and heptagon edges both approach the diameter/equality conditions, giving a natural 2-parameter family to sweep (e.g., 20x20 grid over r in [0.5,1.5], h in [0.2,1.5]). Similarly add the heptagonal prism (14 vertices), the gyroelongated pentagonal bipyramid family, and the 14-vertex Johnson-solids. Critically, after picking each (r,h) analytically compute dmin and dmax and only homotopy-refine the top-k grid entries — this avoids wasting budget on bad parameterizations. Feed these seeds through the existing homotopy solver but with the improved initial t set to the analytic ratio, so bisection starts tight. This directly explores topologies the current program never touches, and the known best solutions for the related n=14 diameter-constrained packing often have antiprism-like local structure.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score (dmin/dmax)^2 via structurally new candidate optima
active_paradigms.cautions: Sweep the parameter grid cheaply with pure numpy distance computations before invoking L-BFGS; ensure the antiprism is built with exact vertex coordinates (r*cos(2*pi*k/7 + phase), r*sin(...), ±h/2) with the 7-fold twist of pi/7 for the antiprism; keep the wall-clock budget guard; normalize each seed to unit diameter before homotopy.

active_paradigms.idea: Directly solve the constrained NLP 'maximize t subject to d(i,j)^2 >= t, d(i,j)^2 <= 1' with scipy.optimize.minimize using method='trust-constr' and analytic Jacobian constraint matrices
active_paradigms.description: The evaluator's own reformulation suggests the natural formulation: variables are the 42 point coordinates plus t, maximize t (minimize -t) with 91 lower-bound and 91 upper-bound nonlinear pairwise-distance constraints. Unlike the current penalty homotopy, trust-constr handles these constraints natively with the interior-point/SQP filter method, staying on the feasible manifold and giving KKT-quality stationary points. Compute the constraint Jacobians analytically: for constraint g_ij = d(i,j)^2 - t >= 0, d/dx_i = 2(x_i - x_j), d/dt = -1; similarly for the upper bounds. Add tiny regularization or a symmetry anchor (fix first point at origin, second on x-axis, third in xy-plane) to remove the 6 rigid-motion degrees of freedom, which dramatically improves conditioning. Run this from the top ~10 seeds found by the existing seeding code (this is deterministic setup, one optimization per seed), then take the best t. This converges to exact local optima of the true problem rather than approximate penalty minimizers, which typically leaves 1e-4 to 1e-3 of ratio on the table.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score by finding exact KKT points of the true constrained problem
active_paradigms.cautions: Scaling matters: work with squared distances and normalize so coordinates are O(1); set gtol=1e-12, xtol=1e-14; provide both constraints as a single vector-valued function with a dense 182x43 Jacobian; the rigid-motion anchoring must be consistent (not all points collinear); fall back to SLSQP if trust-constr stalls; keep total runtime under the budget by limiting to ~10 starts with maxiter=2000.

active_paradigms.idea: Replace bisection homotopy with a smooth annealed surrogate: optimize the differentiable log-sum-exp softmin/softmax of squared distances with L-BFGS, sharpening the temperature schedule to recover the exact ratio
active_paradigms.description: The exact ratio dmin/dmax is non-smooth (argmin/argmax switching), which is why the current hill-climb and penalty approach struggle near the optimum. Define a smooth surrogate S_beta(p) = -logsumexp(-beta * d^2)/beta divided by logsumexp(beta * d^2)/beta (a smooth lower/upper approximation of min and max of squared distances). For moderate beta this is fully differentiable with a closed-form gradient (softmax weights over pairs), so scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' and jac=True can optimize it robustly. Start at beta ~ 2 (very smooth landscape, no local-minimum switching) and anneal beta upward (x2 each stage, up to ~500), warm-starting each stage from the previous solution; as beta grows the surrogate converges monotonically to the true ratio, and the smooth early stages guide the optimizer across the non-smooth kinks that trap the current code. Run this annealing chain from each of the top graph seeds and generic seeds; finish with a few exact-ratio polish steps. Because the surrogate gradient distributes weight over ALL near-minimal and near-maximal pairs simultaneously, it naturally resolves the degenerate contact graphs where multiple pairs tie at dmin and dmax — exactly the structure of the optimum.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score by smoothing the non-smooth min/max objective to escape kink-induced local optima
active_paradigms.cautions: Use scipy.special.logsumexp with beta-scaled inputs to avoid overflow; normalize points to unit diameter at each annealing stage to keep scale fixed (the surrogate is scale-sensitive); gradient uses softmax weights w_ij = exp(beta*(c - d_ij^2)) over the 91 pairs — assemble via np.add.at like the existing penalty gradient; choose per-stage convergence ftol=1e-16 so stages fully converge before sharpening; guard total time; verify the final exact ratio after annealing and keep the best over all chains.

tried_paradigms.idea: Optimize the squared-distance feasibility problem directly with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') using nonlinear constraints d(i,j)^2 >= t and d(i,j)^2 <= 1, maximizing t as an extra variable.
tried_paradigms.description: Reformulate exactly as the evaluator hints: variables are the 42 point coordinates plus t; constraints are 91 lower bounds d^2 - t >= 0 and 91 upper bounds 1 - d^2 >= 0, all smooth quadratics with analytic Jacobians. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr', minimizing -t, supplying NonlinearConstraint objects with vectorized constraint functions and precomputed sparse Jacobians (each constraint involves only 6 coordinates). Warm-start from the current best configuration (which already achieves ratio ~0.4898) and from structured seeds. Because trust-constr handles the KKT conditions of the true feasibility NLP, it can push t past what penalty-based L-BFGS homotopy reaches, since penalty methods leave a small feasibility gap. Increase t incrementally (t += 1e-5) re-solving each time, an exact feasible ascent on the certified lower bound. Guard with time checks and return the best feasible configuration normalized to unit diameter.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / benchmark; directly maximizes the certified lower bound t
tried_paradigms.cautions: Provide analytic Jacobians (2*(xi-xj) pattern) and use sparse LinearConstraint-style sparsity via NonlinearConstraint with jac returning sparse matrices for speed; verify final feasibility numerically (all distances in [t,1]-1e-9) before returning; keep total runtime under the timeout by limiting major iterations per t-step.

tried_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping on the exact ratio objective using scipy.optimize.basinhopping with a min-max aware step generator.
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping on the objective f(p) = -(dmin/dmax) with a custom take_step that moves the point participating in the currently shortest or longest edge along the pair direction (the gradient-informative directions), plus occasional random rotations of the whole configuration (invariance-aware moves that don't change the objective but help escape basins when combined with perturbation). Each basin-hopping iteration locally minimizes with L-BFGS-B on a smooth surrogate: maximize sum of softmin distances, e.g. objective -logsumexp(-d/eps) combined with diameter penalty, which approximates the true nonsmooth ratio well for small eps. Run multiple seeds including the known good structured seeds (icosahedron+2 poles, double hexagon rings). The key difference from the current hill-climb is acceptance of worsening moves (Metropolis) enabling escape from the local optimum at ratio ~0.4898.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary (dmin/dmax)^2 via the smooth surrogate and exact ratio evaluation at the end
tried_paradigms.cautions: The true ratio is nonsmooth; always do final local polish on the exact ratio; set temperature adaptively (accept ~20-30%); use fixed seed; enforce time budget by capping niter based on elapsed time per iteration.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exploit graph/geometric structure: parameterize candidate 14-point configurations by distance-graph topology and search over contact graphs with a force-balance (Stress majorization / spectral) solver.
tried_paradigms.description: At the optimum, the shortest and longest distances form contact graphs. Enumerate plausible topologies: e.g., 14 vertices as two staggered hexagonal rings plus 2 poles (best known candidates), or icosahedron-based capsid structures. For a hypothesized graph with prescribed edge lengths all equal to 1 (both min and max contacts at 1), solve the graph realization / stress equilibrium: find coordinates where each vertex is in equilibrium under unit forces along its contact edges (a first-order condition of the optimum). Implement as fixed-point iteration: each point moves to the weighted centroid of its graph neighbors (stress majorization à la scipy-free implementation, or use scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs on the stress matrix). Then verify and hill-climb. Additionally try spectral placement: use the eigenvectors of the contact-graph Laplacian as initial 3D embedding, then refine. This explores fundamentally different geometric structures than random repulsion seeds.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score by discovering a better contact topology than the current best local optimum
tried_paradigms.cautions: Graph realization may not exist for a hypothesized topology; check all pairwise distances and discard infeasible realizations; keep several topologies within time budget; use fixed seeds for any randomized refinement.
